facts.claim: Air molecules (N2, O2) are much smaller than visible wavelengths (~1000x per NOAA) and scatter short wavelengths more (Rayleigh scattering, intensity ~ 1/lambda^4).
spoken: Air molecules are about a thousand times smaller than a light wave
tiny things scatter short waves far more than long ones

facts.claim: Blue (~450 nm) is scattered about 4x more than red (~650 nm). (650/450)^4 = 4.35; 3.7x for 625 nm.
facts.caveat: NOAA says three to four times (violet vs red); 450 vs 650 nm gives 4.35
spoken: Blue gets bounced around about four times more than red

facts.claim: At sunrise/sunset light crosses far more atmosphere (Brailey Sims estimate ~30x more than overhead), so blue is scattered out of the direct beam and orange/red remain.
spoken: the light reaching you crosses dozens of times more air

facts.claim: The blue removed from a sunset beam contributes to the blue sky seen elsewhere ('sunsets are red because the daytime sky is blue').
facts.caveat: framing simplification: the same scattering seen from another angle, per Met Office
spoken: Both are the same trick, seen from two places
off to color someone else's afternoon
Your sunset is the leftovers of someone else's blue sky

sources.title: Leibniz Univ. Hannover: 'more than four times'
